title: GPU Scale-Model Simulation
problem: Architectural simulation of large-scale GPU systems is time-consuming and resource-intensive, with simulator and infrastructure limitations preventing simulation of systems with increasing numbers of SMs, caches, and bandwidth. GPU applications exhibit vastly different scaling behaviors, breaking traditional one-size-fits-all regression models.
motivation: Efficient performance prediction is critical for evaluating and designing next-generation large-scale GPU systems without requiring expensive full-scale simulation.
method: This method measures how an application performs on two smaller GPU setups—with 8 and 16 streaming multiprocessors (SMs, the cores that run the computations)—and records how often the fast cache memory fails to provide requested data (this pattern is called the miss rate curve). Using these patterns observed from small systems, it can predict how the application will perform on much larger GPU systems without needing to simulate them directly. This works because each application's pattern of cache misses is unique to how it accesses memory, so using application-specific patterns beats using generic prediction formulas that would be wrong for many apps.
key_novelty: You can predict a large-scale GPU system's performance by measuring each application's unique cache-miss pattern on small systems, eliminating the need to simulate the actual large system.
contributions: Novel GPU scale-model methodology that handles application-specific scaling behavior without requiring target system simulators
Achieves 4% average error (max 17%) predicting 128-SM strong-scaling performance using 8-SM and 16-SM scale models
Achieves 1.7% average error (max 4.5%) for weak-scaling prediction with 9.3× simulation speedup
Extends to multi-chiplet GPU performance prediction with 2.5% average error (max 4.3%)

metrics.accuracy: 4% avg error (17% max) strong-scaling; 1.7% avg error (4.5% max) weak-scaling; 2.5% avg error (4.3% max) multi-chiplet

primary_theme: GPU performance prediction via scale-model simulation
